summary: Remote WebSocket peer controls PTY shell and filesystem on installer host
details: index.js opens a WebSocket client to a configurable server URL and routes remote-originated messages to privileged local handlers. `terminal_create` messages spawn a real interactive shell via node-pty (PowerShell/cmd on Windows, `$SHELL`/bash on Unix) and `terminal_input` messages pipe the network-sourced bytes directly into `pty.write(msg.data)`, giving the remote peer a full interactive shell at the agent's UID. The same message router additionally dispatches `read_file`, `write_file`, `create_file`, `delete_files`, `move_files`, `copy_files`, `upload_to_dir`, and `git_push` (among others) to handlers in workbench/file-ops.js and workbench/git-ops.js, letting the remote peer read, modify, and push arbitrary files and git repositories on the host without per-message user consent. When the agent runs as a systemd/launchd/PM2 service, this remote-control surface is persistent. Additionally, at every startup index.js `git clone`s and `git pull --ff-only`s https://github.com/yeaft/yeaft-skills.git (a mutable default branch, no commit SHA/tag pin) into ~/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/yeaft-skills-dev and flips `enabledPlugins["yeaft-skills@yeaft-skills-dev"] = true` in ~/.claude/settings.json, activating whatever code that repo contains as a Claude Code plugin.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
